clue.text: Honoured like Douglas Bader, so to speak

definitions.meaning: kept in mind and commemorated, as the fallen are each November

definitions.text: like Douglas Bader, so to speak
definitions.meaning: the RAF pilot Douglas Bader lost both legs and flew again on artificial ones, so jokingly he was given limbs again, 're-limbed'

explanation.surface: A tribute to the legless wartime fighter ace, as people still talk of him.
explanation.walkthrough: The second reading splits the word as RE-MEMBERED: provided with members (limbs) once more, as the double-amputee Bader was.
explanation.definitionFit: To be commemorated is to be held in memory, the same idea as being honoured.

clue.text: English word of address summoning up bygone age

parts.note: the vocative is the grammatical case used when addressing someone directly

explanation.surface: An English phrase of greeting that conjures up the past.
explanation.definitionFit: Something evocative calls a past era vividly to mind.

clue.text: King of England has risen in anger, imprisoning duke

indicators.note: the turned word holds the next piece inside it, like a cell around a prisoner
in a down clue, rising means the word is read from the bottom upwards, so backwards

parts.note: anger means rage

explanation.surface: An English monarch flies into a fury and locks up a nobleman.
explanation.walkthrough: 'has risen' turns RAGE into EGAR, and 'imprisoning' puts D inside it after the first letter. Edgar was a tenth-century English king.
explanation.definitionFit: Several Anglo-Saxon rulers bore this name, notably Edgar the Peaceful.

clue.text: Musicians wanting money not allowed to audition

parts.note: brass is British slang for money

indicators.note: an audition is a hearing, so the word for 'not allowed' is taken as it sounds when heard

parts.note: not allowed means banned

explanation.surface: Performers, short of cash, are barred from trying out for a part.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to audition' signals that BANNED is to be heard, giving the same sound as BAND. Brass for money is British slang.
explanation.definitionFit: A brass band is a group of players of trumpets, cornets and the like.

clue.text: Socialist rebelled, showing an emblem of war

parts.note: red is the traditional colour, and a byword, for a socialist
rose, as in rose up, means rebelled

explanation.surface: A left-winger revolted, displaying a battle symbol.
explanation.walkthrough: The war is the Wars of the Roses, the fifteenth-century English civil war in which Lancaster's badge was a red flower.
explanation.definitionFit: The House of Lancaster's badge in the Wars of the Roses was this flower.

clue.text: Scheme to replace roof of porter's house?

annotationWithheld.why: Clue held as 'Scheme to replace roof of porter's house? (5)': LODGE with its top letter changed gives DODGE, but nothing in the clue as held supplies the D; a word is missing and searches found no other text.
annotationWithheld.clue: Scheme to replace roof of porter's house?

clue.text: Old PM joining in tributes

indicators.note: the answer sits inside the letters of the next word

explanation.surface: A former prime minister joins in the paying of tributes.
explanation.walkthrough: The Earl of Bute was British prime minister in 1762-63.
explanation.definitionFit: John Stuart, Earl of Bute, led the British government under George III.

clue.text: Rising young scout can always become an adventurer

indicators.note: in a down clue, rising means the word is written from the bottom upwards

parts.note: a cub is a junior member of the Scout movement
taken as written
e'er is the poetic contraction of ever, meaning always

explanation.surface: An up-and-coming junior scout can always grow into a daring explorer.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Rising' turns CUB into BUC. E'ER, the poetic shortening of ever, supplies the ending.
explanation.definitionFit: A buccaneer was a pirate, a seafaring adventurer of the Caribbean.

clue.text: Light vehicle seen in Pacific islands

definitions.meaning: a light two-wheeled horse-drawn carriage used in India
a Polynesian kingdom made up of many islands

explanation.surface: A small carriage spotted on South Sea islands.
explanation.definitionFit: The word names both an Indian pony cart and a Polynesian island kingdom.

clue.text: Wish to have assistance for writing

parts.note: to long is to wish
a hand is help, as in 'give me a hand'

explanation.surface: Someone wants help with their handwriting.
explanation.definitionFit: This is ordinary handwriting, as opposed to shorthand or typing.

clue.text: Impression about church being respectable

indicators.note: the first piece goes round the second, as about can mean surrounding

parts.note: a dent is an impression in a surface
CE is the Church of England

explanation.surface: An impression formed about a church is that it is respectable.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' signals that the word for impression surrounds the church abbreviation.
explanation.definitionFit: A decent person is proper and of good standing.

clue.text: Boatman in southern part of Hebridean island

definitions.meaning: One of the rowers in Jerome K Jerome's comic novel Three Men in a Boat
Lewis and ... is one island in the Outer Hebrides, its southern section bearing this name

explanation.surface: A ferryman working on the southern end of a Scottish island.
explanation.walkthrough: The boatman is not a ferryman but one of the trio in Three Men in a Boat (1889). The Hebrides are islands off Scotland's west coast.
explanation.definitionFit: The name belongs both to a character in Jerome's boating novel and to the southern part of Lewis.

clue.text: Atop her, a collapsible accessory — atop him surely?

indicators.note: something collapsible folds into a new shape, so the preceding letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A lady's folding item, though surely it belongs on a gentleman's head.
explanation.walkthrough: 'collapsible' rearranges ATOPHERA. An opera hat is a collapsible top hat, so it sits atop a man, not a woman.
explanation.definitionFit: A gentleman's opera hat is a folding top hat worn with evening dress.

clue.text: Greeting some of Hitler's men showing contempt?

definitions.note: the clue's phrase stands for a sound of scorn, a noun rather than a participle

parts.note: hi is a greeting
the SS was the Nazi paramilitary force

explanation.surface: Saluting a group of Nazi soldiers in a disdainful way.
explanation.walkthrough: The question mark admits that the definition describes what the answer does rather than naming it exactly.
explanation.definitionFit: Audiences make this sibilant noise to express scorn for a villain or a poor performance.

clue.text: Have wine for sale in northern town

parts.note: to stock goods is to have them for sale, and 'for sale' completes that sense
port is a fortified wine

explanation.surface: Keep wine available for purchase in a town up north.
explanation.walkthrough: 'for sale' belongs with 'Have': to stock is to have for sale. Stockport is a town near Manchester.
explanation.definitionFit: Stockport is a large town in Greater Manchester in the north of England.

clue.text: Momentary lapse, holding note, using wind instrument?

indicators.note: the rearranged letters keep the note inside them
a lapse is a slip or fall, so the letters of the first word slip out of order

parts.note: E is a musical note

explanation.surface: A brief slip of concentration while sustaining a note on a wind instrument.
explanation.walkthrough: 'lapse' rearranges the first word's letters into ANMOMETRY, and 'holding' says the note sits within that jumble. The definition jokes that a gauge for breezes is a wind instrument.
explanation.definitionFit: Measuring air speed with an anemometer, a gauge for breezes, is this science.

clue.text: Carelessness made public groan inwardly

indicators.note: the second piece goes into the middle of the first

parts.note: overt means openly displayed
a sigh is a low groan

explanation.surface: Negligence was exposed, and people groaned to themselves.
explanation.walkthrough: 'inwardly' says the groan goes inside the word for made public; 'groan inwardly' reads in the surface as suppressed dismay.
explanation.definitionFit: An oversight is a slip made through lack of attention.

clue.text: Little woman held in check, beloved denied a retort

indicators.note: the woman is kept inside the word for check

parts.note: to rein is to check, and a rein is a check
Jo March is one of the sisters in Louisa May Alcott's novel Little Women

indicators.note: the word for beloved is deprived of the letter that follows

parts.note: dear means beloved

explanation.surface: A small lady is restrained and her sweetheart refuses a comeback.
explanation.walkthrough: 'held in' and 'denied' are the two signals; 'Little woman' points to Alcott's novel, not to a small person.
explanation.definitionFit: A rejoinder is a sharp reply, the same as a retort.

clue.text: Naval officer back with wife?

parts.note: to second is to back or support
a mate is a spouse

explanation.surface: Someone asks whether a sailor is returning with his spouse.
explanation.definitionFit: A second mate is the officer next below the first mate on a merchant ship.

clue.text: Dancer almost ditching one, the heartless goddess!

indicators.note: ditching means getting rid of the letter for one
almost means the last letter is dropped from the name

parts.note: Fred Astaire was the celebrated Hollywood dancer
I is the Roman numeral for one

indicators.note: heartless means the middle letter of the little word is removed

explanation.surface: A dancer nearly gives up a partner, crying out against the cruel goddess.
explanation.walkthrough: 'almost' cuts ASTAIRE to ASTAIR, 'ditching' drops its I to leave ASTAR, and 'heartless' takes H from THE, leaving TE.
explanation.definitionFit: Astarte was the Phoenician goddess of fertility and love.

clue.text: Ruler not in harmony after revolution

indicators.note: a revolution turns something round, so the word is read backwards

parts.note: ajar can mean out of harmony, jarring

explanation.surface: A ruler loses the people's support after an uprising.
explanation.walkthrough: 'after revolution' turns AJAR back to front. Ajar here means jarring, discordant, not half open.
explanation.definitionFit: A raja is an Indian king or prince.

clue.text: Second murder demanded police surveillance

parts.note: to take out someone is slang for killing them

explanation.surface: A second killing called for officers to keep watch.
explanation.definitionFit: A stakeout is a covert police watch on a place or person.

clue.text: Time on instrument of torture — one may well be beaten

parts.note: the rack stretched its victims

explanation.surface: A spell on the torture rack: someone could easily be beaten.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition plays on the phrase 'a well-beaten track', a path trodden by many feet.
explanation.definitionFit: A path becomes beaten by repeated trampling, so a well-used route is well beaten.

clue.text: Nothing in the existing circumstances can provide welcome relief

parts.note: O, the zero, means nothing
as is means in the present state, as it stands

explanation.surface: Nothing in the present situation can offer a welcome break.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in' puts O inside AS IS, after its first A.
explanation.definitionFit: An oasis is figuratively a refreshing respite amid hardship, like a watered spot in a desert.

clue.text: Male and maiden in costume for important meeting

indicators.note: the two letters go inside the word for costume

parts.note: a suit is a costume or outfit
M stands for maiden, an over with no runs, on a cricket scorecard

explanation.surface: A man and a young woman in fancy dress attend a key gathering.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in' puts MM inside SUIT. M for maiden is the cricket scorer's mark for an over with no runs.
explanation.definitionFit: A summit is a high-level conference between leaders.

clue.text: The man keeping account brought up an old book

indicators.note: in a down clue, brought up means the whole is written from the bottom upwards
the first word keeps the second inside it

parts.note: him is a word for the man

explanation.surface: A fellow holding a ledger produced an ancient volume.
explanation.walkthrough: 'keeping' puts one piece inside the other to give HACIM, and 'brought up', in a down clue, turns that whole result round.
explanation.definitionFit: Micah is one of the minor prophets of the Old Testament.

clue.text: Nothing is just right initially it's the dialect

indicators.note: initially says the piece for just right comes first, ahead of the other two

parts.note: pat means exactly right, apt
O, the zero, means nothing

explanation.surface: Nothing is quite correct at first in this local speech.
explanation.walkthrough: 'initially' puts PAT ahead of O and IS, though they come first in the clue.
explanation.definitionFit: A patois is a regional variety of speech, often non-standard.

clue.text: For instance, one group of police coming in about murder of top man

indicators.note: the three pieces come into the word for about

parts.note: re means about, concerning
e.g. means for instance
I is the Roman numeral for one
the CID is the Criminal Investigation Department, Britain's detective branch

explanation.surface: One squad of detectives arrives to look into the killing of the boss.
explanation.walkthrough: 'coming in' signals that three pieces enter the word for about. The CID is the British detective branch.
explanation.definitionFit: Regicide is the killing of a king, the man at the very top.

clue.text: Taking off woman's garment's not right!

indicators.note: not here means without, so the following letter is removed

parts.note: a skirt is a woman's garment

explanation.surface: Removing a woman's skirt is improper!
explanation.walkthrough: 'not' removes R (right) from SKIRT. 'Taking off' means a parody, not undressing.
explanation.definitionFit: A skit is a short comic parody, a take-off.

clue.text: Swarthiest characters wandering around in casual gear

indicators.note: wandering letters move about, so the word's letters are reordered

explanation.surface: The darkest-skinned people strolling about in relaxed clothing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'wandering around' rearranges the letters of SWARTHIEST; 'characters' says those letters are what moves.
explanation.definitionFit: A loose cotton jersey is everyday informal clothing.
